Hi Priya —

Thanks again for the demo last week. The execs asked us to fast-track a private offer for our pilot. We reviewed the two pricing flavors you shared (flat-pack reserved capacity vs metered per-token Turbo bundle) and have a couple of follow-ups before we give procurement the green light:

1) Channel margin — our reseller (Edge Systems) needs clarity on a pass-through commission and how it will appear on the Azure invoice. Are you able to structure a 12% reseller fee that is either shown as a separate line or achieved via a managed passback?

2) Usage floor — CloudScale's finance team wants a 1,000k token monthly floor (for month-to-month billing) to avoid per-month volatility; how does that interact with your batching/caching assumptions?

3) SKU mapping — can you map the Turbo bundle into a single Marketplace SKU for easier procurement entry, or does Azure require the reserved capacity and metered components to be separate line items?

Attached: RDW-3421-pricing-matrix.xlsx (our initial numbers).

We'd like to get a draft DocuSign this week if possible.

Best,
Sarah

Hi Sarah —

Appreciate the clear asks — looping in Ben (go-to-market pricing) and Mina (deal ops) to confirm operational detail. Quick answers up-front:

- We can do a 12% reseller pass-through in one of two ways: (A) show a separate invoice line as a rebate from Redwood to Edge (requires reseller onboarding ticket with Azure to route the line) or (B) bake the commission into the private-offer net price and provide a commission statement to Edge for reconciliation. Option A is cleaner for your accounting team.

- 1,000k token floor is fine; it interacts with our autoscaling and cache assumptions only insofar as it sets a minimum monthly charge — we can reflect a blended effective $/k token in the private offer to smooth the economics.

- SKU mapping: Azure prefers discrete SKUs for reserved vs metered. That said, we can publish a single umbrella SKU that expands to two internal line-items in the Marketplace listing; purchasers will see one SKU but the private-offer will reference the underlying components. That keeps procurement simple while preserving accurate metering.

Ben/Mina — can you take the attachment and produce a final pricing matrix that (1) shows the invoice presentation options for Edge, (2) calculates the blended $/k under a 1,000k floor, and (3) produces an Azure-friendly SKU bundle name? Sarah — we'll aim to have a draft doc and a DocuSign link by EOD Thursday.

Thanks,
Priya
Priya Natarajan
Head of Sales, Cloud Partners
Redwood Inference

Priya / Sarah —

I pulled the sheet and ran three scenarios; summary below and attached a cleaned matrix (I renamed a few columns). Notes:

1) Invoice presentation (Option A vs B):
   - Option A (separate reseller commission line): Azure invoice will show Redwood list price, private-offer discount, then a reseller rebate line. Requires our partner ops to file a reseller routing request with Azure marketplace (3–5 business days to confirm path).
   - Option B (commission embedded): Simpler to activate immediately; Edge gets a commission statement from us monthly. Downside: not itemized on the Azure invoice, which some finance teams dislike.

2) Blended pricing under 1,000k floor:
   - Flat-pack reserved capacity (monthly): conservatively priced at $X.XX /k tokens equivalent after amortization.
   - Metered Turbo bundle: base per-token is $Y.YY/k; with the 1,000k floor the effective blended rate (assuming baseline use == floor) sits ~5–8% above reserved amortized price due to burst headroom.

3) SKU recommendation: Suggested umbrella SKU: RDW-TURBO-FLATPACK-1000 (displays as "Redwood Turbo Pilot: Flatpack+Metered" in the Marketplace). Under the hood map to two internal line items: TURBO-RESV-01 and TURBO-MTR-01.

Action items I can take: finalize matrix, estimate Azure reseller routing lead time, and draft the private-offer PDF with the selected invoice option. Mina — can you confirm if we have any tax/regulatory constraints for showing separate commission lines in NA?

Attachment: RDW-3421-pricing-matrix.xlsx (cleaned).

Ben
